subject: SLA tiering and credit cap proposal for NimbusPay integration
messages:
From: Maya Diaz <maya@nubispay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA expectations for NimbusPay integration

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks good and the team is excited to move forward. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of constraints so we can get a sensible SLA baked into the commercial agreement:

- For our payments clearing flows we need a 99.98% uptime commitment for primary endpoints, but we are open to tiering non-critical batch endpoints to 99.9%.
- We want a hard cap on monthly service credits — our legal team is pushing back on open-ended exposure. Ideally a cap equal to 30% of monthly fees.
- A carveout for scheduled maintenance is acceptable, but we want a max of 6 hours/month of scheduled maintenance that can be excluded from uptime calculations.

Can Redwood provide a template that reflects the tiering described above? Also attaching our initial procurement checklist (see attachment reference). If you could send a redline we’ll have our procurement lawyer look it over.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Maya Diaz
Head of Integrations, NimbusPay

Attachment: nubis-procurement-checklist.pdf (reference)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Diaz <maya@nubispay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 12:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA expectations for NimbusPay integration

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Quick thoughts and a counterproposal to keep both sides comfortable while moving the deal forward:⁠

1) Baseline uptime: we can commit to 99.95% for all API endpoints across the hosted Redwood platform. For the payment-critical endpoints we can offer an optional "priority tier" at 99.98% if NimbusPay agrees to a small dedicated-capacity premium (this would be part of the Dedicated offering).

2) Monthly credit cap: we propose a two-tier cap instead of a single flat number: 40% of monthly fees for the first 6 months after go‑live (to give NimbusPay protection during ramp) then 25% thereafter, with a 3‑month rolling aggregate cap equal to 60% to avoid concentrated clawbacks. This gives protection but limits open-ended liability on our side.

3) Maintenance carveouts: we can carve out scheduled maintenance up to 4 hours/month (not 6) for routine infra work; anything beyond that would count against uptime unless we schedule it as a customer-approved maintenance window. We also propose a 48-hour advance notice for any non-emergency maintenance.

4) Regional fallbacks / incident routing: if an incident is isolated to a single region, credits apply only to usage billed in that region.

I’m attaching a proposed redline with these items (redlines-proposed-sla.docx). Ben, can you confirm whether the dedicated premium estimate for the priority tier is acceptable?

Next steps: if NimbusPay is broadly ok with the structure, we’ll send a formal redline (DocuSign‑ready) and ask for legal to mark up the few outstanding items.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0147

Attachment: redlines-proposed-sla.docx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: internal: NimbusPay negotiation playbook

Ben / Laura — quick internal note so we’re aligned before sending the redline to Maya this afternoon:

- Objective: preserve our exposure while giving NimbusPay the frictionless guarantee they want for payments-critical traffic. Offer will be hybrid (hosted default 99.95 + paid 99.98 priority tier).
- Credits calculus: ask legal to sign off on 40% initial cap then 25% thereafter; emphasize the 3-month rolling cap as a dealbreaker for us.
- Maintain 4-hr scheduled maintenance carveout; push back on 6-hr ask.
- If they insist on 99.98 for primary endpoints without dedicated capacity, we should require a stricter credit cap (15%) and limited SLA scope.

I’ll send the redline to Maya this afternoon. HubSpot deal ID 9876543 — please update stage to "SLA Negotiation".

Tessa

From: Samir Kaur <samir.kaur@nubispay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Diaz <maya@nubispay.com>, NimbusPay Procurement <procurement@nubispay.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: SLA expectations for NimbusPay integration

Tessa — thanks for the quick reply and the concrete structure. A few counterpoints from procurement/legal after an internal sync:

- Tiering: good starting point. NimbusPay prefers 99.98 for payments-critical endpoints on hosted (no dedicated premium) because our current stack runs across multiple cloud providers and we need parity in guarantees.
- Credit cap: we are open to a stepped cap, but 40% initial then 25% later is higher than our negotiating mandate. Can you do 30% initial then 20% thereafter? Also we need the cap to be per-service rather than global (we run multiple contracts).
- Maintenance carveout: we can accept 4 hours/month carveout if Redwood commits to a quarterly maintenance calendar with at least one planned window per quarter.

Attached are our redlines (nimbuspay-redlines.pdf). Highlighted: request 99.98 for primary endpoints without dedicated premium, and a per-service cap of 30%/20%.

If Redwood cannot accept 99.98 without dedicated capacity, we’ll likely accept your hybrid approach if you can move the initial cap to 30% and keep the per-service cap model.

Thanks —
Samir Kaur
Procurement Manager, NimbusPay
Attachment: nimbuspay-redlines.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kaur <samir.kaur@nubispay.com>, Maya Diaz <maya@nubispay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA tiering and credit cap proposal for NimbusPay integration

Samir / Maya — thanks for the notes and for sending the redlines. We want to keep the commercial process moving, so here’s a final compromise we can accept for the MSA addendum:

- Primary endpoints: 99.98 SLA for payments-critical endpoints on hosted (no dedicated premium) limited to a "defined subset" of endpoints (we will enumerate them in the SOW). This is contingent on a joint runbook and operational onboarding (playbooks, runbooks, on-call contacts).
- Credit cap: per-service cap of 30% for the first 6 months post‑go-live, then 20% thereafter; 3‑month rolling aggregate cap of 60% remains in place.
- Maintenance carveout: 4 hours/month carveout accepted; Redwood will provide a quarterly maintenance calendar and 48 hours advance notice for non-emergency maintenance.
- Incident scope: regional incidents will have credits applied only to usage from the impacted region.

If you confirm in writing we’ll incorporate these items into the DocuSign-ready SLA addendum and route to your legal team. Attaching the redline we’ll send to DocuSign once NimbusPay confirms final language (redlines-proposed-sla.docx).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0147

Attachment: redlines-proposed-sla.docx
